question: What are the design features and operational parameters of high-temperature and low-temperature plasma reactors used for reactive nitrogen species production?
answer: The nitrogen pentoxide production system utilizes two distinct plasma reactors.  The high-temperature (HT) reactor employs a double concentric glass/quartz tube design with a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) powered by 13.6 kVp-p AC at 12.5 kHz, generating approximately 44 W of power. This design, incorporating countercurrent heat exchange, prioritizes nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) production. The low-temperature (LT) reactor also uses a DBD configuration, operating at ~7.8 kVp-p and ~5.7 kHz with a power of 3.4 W.  This lower power favors ozone (O3) generation. Both reactors maintain a constant airflow of 1 L/min.

### Task 1: Summarize the purpose of the paper in clear and concise terms  
The paper aims to develop a novel synthesis method for dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) using air and electricity via discharge plasmas, eliminating the need for hazardous raw materials. The authors demonstrate the nitrating capability of the N2O5-rich plasma effluent gas on tyrosine, highlighting its potential for widespread scientific and industrial applications.
